origem: Reviewer request, round 1 (MDPI Mathematics), Reviewer 2, item 3: 'Report the contributing cluster counts and assess suitable small-sample alternatives'
pergunta: Do small-sample alternatives repair the coverage of the interval of ONE partition? Same data as R5: 16 cells, g=10 km, b=2 km, 60 draws (fase5/_parcial_laco/<cell>.json: S_B and M_B per test block, predictors constante and fspl_b, populations validos and todos). Coverage target: the mean of Err over the draws where Err is defined (primary reading A of R5).
metodo_fixado: Per draw, with k = test blocks with M_B>0 and N = N_blocos_ocupados: (a) R5 base: Err +- 2 sqrt(v), v = (1-k/N) k/(k-1) sum_B (S_B - Err M_B)^2 / M^2 (reproduce R5 as a check; it must match fase5/R5_resumo.json); (b) t: Err +- t_{0.975; k-1} sqrt(v); (c) block jackknife: Err_(-B) = (S - S_B)/(M - M_B), v_jk = (k-1)/k sum_B (Err_(-B) - mean_B)^2, intervals Err +- 2 sqrt(v_jk) and Err +- t_{k-1} sqrt(v_jk); (d) wild cluster bootstrap: r_B = S_B - Err M_B; R = 999 replicates with Rademacher weights w_B, Err* = Err + sum_B w_B r_B / M, percentile interval 2.5-97.5 and symmetric interval Err +- t_{k-1} sd(Err*); seed 20261026. Draws with k<2 are undefined and counted. Per cell/predictor/population: coverage of each interval, Q of each variance estimator (mean over draws / empirical variance of Err between draws), median and range of k, number of blocks of the cell with a valid node (fase5/blocos_com_no_valido.json). Summary table over the 16 cells x {constante, fspl_b} x {validos, todos}.
previsao: Partial: t_{k-1} with k between 2 and 20 widens little (t_16 = 2.12); the jackknife and the wild bootstrap capture the variance BETWEEN blocks of one draw, not the randomness of the population scored by the trimming, which the Q = 0.51 of R5 says is about half of the between-draw variance in the valid nodes.
leitura: constante, validos: some method (b)-(d) with coverage >= 0.90 in >= 12 of the 16 cells -> REPAIRS (DELIMITS S9 under a favourable condition): the undercoverage was a small-sample effect; the reporting rule adopts the method that repaired it. All methods with coverage < 0.80 in >= 8 cells -> DOES NOT REPAIR (REINFORCES S9 and S4): the single-partition estimator, even corrected, does not see the randomness of the population scored; only the distribution over draws measures the drift. In between -> PARTIAL: report the best method, its coverage and the fraction of the gap (1 - base coverage) it closes. In any case the sentence of the Conclusions names the estimator (concession to Reviewer 2).
se_inverter: No outcome reverses S4; REPAIRS delimits S9 (the rule gains the correction).
